title: cross-org inference sprint debrief - nov 13 2025
body:
Context
This note captures the highlights and decisions from the 90-minute cross-org sprint debrief we ran on 2025-11-13. Attendees included engineering (serving runtime, infra, SRE), product (hosted API + dedicated), and solutions eng. Goal was to review the 3-week inference sprint outcomes: KV cache prototype, dynamic batching improvements, and the rollout plan for int8 quantized llama variants.

What shipped in the sprint (summary)
- KV cache v0.2 (prototype): persistent prefix cache + eviction policy tuned for chat workloads. Deployed to canary hosts (canary-12, canary-13). Includes metrics export for hit/miss by customer route.
- Dynamic batcher rewrite: simplifies per-model batching windows, reduces head-of-line locking by using per-shard queues. Observed improved throughput under mixed-latency workloads.
- Quantization experiment: int8 runtime path for 13B Llama-variants integrated; fallback to fp16 when generation quality falls below threshold in monitored evals.

Operational signals observed during canary
- Latency: p50 on canary decreased 6% for 8k context chat prompts; p95 unchanged. p99 spikes still visible for sequences >6k tokens.
- Throughput: tokens/sec increased ~22% on steady-state traffic for simulated 60% chat/40% completion mix.
- Error rate: transient decoding errors observed at ~0.03% on canary-13 during a rolling kernel swap (tracked in JIRA-ENG-2143).
- KV cache hit rates: 38% overall on test traces; hit rate varies widely by customer route (0–72%).

Key decisions and rationale
1) Proceed with staged rollout for KV cache to 20% of serving clusters over next 2 weeks. Rationale: overall hit rate is promising and the cache is safe — eviction policy avoids wrong-prefix returns, and we have metrics to quickly rollback if quality regressions surface. Owners: Priya (runtime), Owen (infra).
2) Keep dynamic batcher in place but enable per-customer policies. Rationale: some enterprise customers benefited from larger batching, but PLG customers need lower latency. Owner: Maya (platform).
3) Delay full int8 rollout for public catalog. Keep int8 behind Dedicated-only flag for now. Rationale: quantization showed small quality regressions on factuality tests; better for closed, validated deployments where customers accept the tradeoff. Owner: Zara (applied-ml).

Open follow-ups (short term)
- Q1: Add model-level cache warming for pinned contexts (owner: Priya) — due 2025-11-27.
- Q2: Instrument per-route quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-style quick checks + hallucination heuristics) to detect quantization regressions automatically (owner: Zara + EngQA) — due 2025-12-11.
- Q3: Incident postmortem for kernel swap errors (JIRA-ENG-2143) — SRE/Release Eng to produce root cause and mitigation by 2025-11-20 (owner: Lucas).
- Q4: Cost analysis: compute marginal token cost delta for int8 vs fp16 across 3 representative SKUs (owner: Finance eng analyst, CC: Maya) — due 2025-11-26.

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: Cache-induced staleness for streaming chat where user edits context quickly. Mitigation: ensure TTL per-tenant and conservative TTL defaults; add client-facing doc and toggle to disable KV cache per-route.
- Risk: Batch consolidation causing tail-latency regressions for small interactive requests. Mitigation: per-customer batch profiles + latency SLO guardrails in the router.
- Risk: Quantization quality regressions outside our eval set. Mitigation: expand eval prompts (see linked Confluence page) and require a pass on the extended eval before enabling int8 for a customer.

Metrics snapshot (canary baseline)
- p50 latency (8k chat) = 74ms (was 79ms pre-sprint)
- p95 latency (8k chat) = 260ms (unchanged)
- p99 latency (long sequences >8k) = 1.9s (spikes during kernel swap)
- Tokens/sec on canary cluster = +22% vs baseline
- Decode error rate = 0.03% (kernel swap windows)
- KV cache hit rate = 38% overall (route distribution: median 29%, 90th 63%)

Notes from breakout discussions
- Applied ML: need stronger signal tying generation quality to routing decisions. If a model variant falls below threshold, router should prefer a more conservative fp16 variant, not just fallback by region.
- Solutions Eng: request a private beta toggle for Dedicated customers to opt-in to int8 with a safety net/rollback window.
- Platform: concern about observability delta — current dashboards lump cache misses with model misses which obscures root causes. Action: split series and add tags (cache_hit=true/false) to request traces (owner: Owen).

Action items (concrete)
- Priya: rollout KV cache to 20% clusters; add per-route disable flag; publish short runbook — due 2025-11-20.
- Owen: split metrics series, add cache_hit tag, and instrument eviction/gc latencies — due 2025-11-18.
- Zara: expand extended eval set, publish quantization quality report for 13B variants — due 2025-11-24.
- Maya: implement per-customer batch policy config in Console UI (design + API spec) — initial proposal due 2025-11-21.
- Lucas: lead incident postmortem and recommend kernel swap best-practices for next rollout — due 2025-11-20.

Customer impact notes
- Two enterprise customers (account ids redacted in notes) were part of the early dinner beta and reported 10–15% cost savings on heavy completion workloads using the dedicated int8 path; however one raised concerns around occasional longer-tail hallucinations. Solutions Eng to coordinate with these accounts to gather more qualitative feedback.

Communication plan
- Internal: short recap + action items posted to #eng-serving-runtime and #platform-product by 2025-11-14 (done).
- Customer-facing (beta): Solutions Eng will draft a private beta email for Dedicated customers offering opt-in to int8 with a one-week guard window; target send 2025-11-21.

Appendix: quick links
- PR with KV cache changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1824
- Batcher rewrite branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/compare/batcher-rewrite
- Kernel-swap incident ticket: JIRA-ENG-2143

If you were at the debrief and have edits or missed items, reply inline or ping Eli. We'll lock this doc and convert to the official sprint retrospective after owners close the short-term action items.
